subject: Edge path instability impacting Valence throughput — exec notified
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@valence.ai>

Cc: infra-ops@valence.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop / 502 spike impacting production

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We're seeing a sharp degradation starting ~07:45 PST across our inference traffic to the Redwood hosted endpoints: token throughput is down ~45%, and 502/504 error rates have spiked to ~8% (normally <0.2%). Tail latency (95p) is up from ~120ms to ~1.2s. This is impacting our web-facing features and page-loads.

We've grabbed a short pcap and some app logs (attached: valence_error_sample-logs.zip). Key observations from our side:
- Errors correlate with requests routed through the us-west-2 peering/VPC leg to your inference pool.
- TCP retransmits and SYN retries visible in the capture around 07:50–08:00.
- We don't see ring-fenced CPU or bursts on our side; backend pods appear healthy.

Can you confirm whether there were any peering/network config changes, or proxy pool adjustments on your side in the last 24 hours? We need immediate mitigation — even a temporary region failover — and an exec-level point of contact.

Thanks,
Carlos
VP Engineering, Valence AI
Attachments: valence_error_sample-logs.zip

I’ll update within 30 minutes with what we see.

—Jonas

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai; lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@valence.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: sudden throughput drop / 502 spike impacting production

Carlos / team — quick triage notes: attaching trace and a sampled flow export (debug-trace-20281009.txt, flow-sample-pcap.txt).

What our initial telemetry shows (us-west-2 edge -> dedicated pool):
- Burst of short-lived TCP sessions with high SYN retry rates between 07:46–08:02.
- DNS lookup latency increased for our internal resolver cluster in the same window (from ~10ms to ~320ms median for some prefixes).
- Firewall/proxy connection pool on the edge proxies (proxy-pset-12) reached connection limit; we see 502 responses when the pool couldn't hand off.
- NAT ephemeral port exhaustion observed on a small subset of egress nodes; ports reclaimed slowly leading to transient failures.

Hypothesis: combination of DNS resolver slowness + proxy connection pool exhaustion leading to failed handoffs and elevated 5xx. NAT port exhaustion amplified the symptom for particular AS paths.

Immediate mitigations we’re executing (in flight):
1) Increase proxy-pset-12 connection threshold by +30% (10m rolling change).
2) Temporarily route new Valence sessions to an alternate pool in us-east-1; this will preserve sessions but may add ~60–80ms RTT for new connections.
3) Rotate DNS resolver endpoints for affected edge nodes to a healthy replica set.
4) Add NAT port reclaim tuning (shorter TIME_WAIT) on the most impacted egress nodes.

If those steps don't drop error rate under 1% within 45 minutes we'll open an urgent peering escalation with the cloud provider (possible link flap or Q-in-Q queuing on the peering leg).

Attachments: debug-trace-20281009.txt, flow-sample-pcap.txt

—Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Team — good triage. A few things to add for the exec deck and customer comms:
- Exec summary (to be shared with CRO/CTO & Valence VP): short description, impact (approx revenue/requests affected per hour), immediate mitigations, and 72h action plan. I’ll draft the note once we confirm mitigation results.
- Customer goodwill: pre-approved concession is one week of usage credit for affected capacity if we can't get to <0.5% 5xx within 24h. Please don't promise anything beyond that without legal sign-off.
- Product/infrastructure asks: Marissa — we need quick instrumentation (one-click) to shift Valence traffic to alternate route for future incidents. This should be a high-priority P1 request for the routing team.

Action owners:
- Marissa: validate whether peering hop shows packet drops (I/O counters) or purely transient queuing (buffer fill). If packet drop, open cloud peering ticket and request packet captures from provider.
- Lauren: coordinate customer updates. Draft a short note to Carlos summarizing steps and ETA.
- Jonas: prep exec note if SLA/renewal impacts emerge.

I'll be on standby and will join any customer call.

—Vivek
VP Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks — team performed the temporary region shift and we can confirm error rate dropped to ~0.9% within 20 minutes. Tail latency is back to ~150ms for most users. Appreciate the rapid response.

Two asks from Valence:
1) We need a substantive post-incident timeline and root cause with concrete mitigations for recurrence (peering resilience, NAT headroom, better health checks).
2) Request a once-weekly sync for the next three weeks to validate stability as we ramp traffic.

I'll attach the additional app logs we captured in case it's helpful (attached: valence_followup-logs.zip).

Carlos

- Product (tracked by Marissa): implement routing toggle (ops-safe) for targeted customer failover — target sprint-by date: 2028-11-02.
- Vivek / Lauren: customer comms and concession details; finalize credit scope if RCA indicates platform responsibility.
- Jonas: prepare exec brief for CRO/CTO by Fri 2028-10-13 12:00 PST.

We have informed Eng leadership and opened a cloud peering ticket referencing our packet samples; Marissa will escalate to provider if we see persistent drops. Great teamwork — let's keep the cadence tight for the RCA.

—Jonas
